conservation.condition_narrative: The canvas is in good plane and tension. There are losses and abrasions along the edges due to direct contact under the historic frames. There is a 4" long scratch (through the varnish) near the bottom of the painting. Another scratch (approximately 1 ½" long), through the paint layer, is located on the right side at 22 ¼" up from the bottom edge. There is a sideways "V"-shape burnish/scrape at the upper right quadrant. All dark brown passages in this area exhibit a mottled, spotty blanching in specular illumination. There are frequent and consistent holidays in the brushwork at the edges of painted forms; these are not damage.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a medium-weight, relatively open, coarsely spun, basket-weave linen canvas over a typical, "American Style" double-bevel-faced, mortise-and-tenon, mitered-corner wood stretcher. All keys (new) are extant and secured for travel. Canvas has been trimmed flush with the verso of the tacking edges. The warps are oriented horizontally. 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** The artist or her assistant appears to have applied a dilute protein size, such as rabbit-skin glue or gelatin, followed by a priming of alternating layers of lead carbonate (PbCO3) in oil and zinc oxide (ZnO) in oil. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** Graphite underdrawing is seldom visible at the margins of adjacent forms. The work is executed in single and double layers of thin, cream-like paints, which have generally leveled to reveal the full texture of the canvas. Brush texture is generally slightly retained in the liquid-to-slightly stiff paints of darker values. There are frequent, linear, raised ridges of paint at the margins of forms. There are often holidays, where the ground of the canvas is visible below, at the margins of forms where one color meets another. Scrubbing or zigzag brushwork has often been used in brighter values. The artist has executed gradual, stepped transitions in value or hue, often painting wet into dry in brief, slightly overlapping bands in a technique suggestive of pastel application. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** An isobutyl methacrylate resin varnish typical for the artist is suspected. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The work is framed in a contemporary micro-environmentally buffered and gasketed, reproduction "L" profile rolled metal frame with brushed steel and lacquered finish with Optium acrylic glazing and new insulated secondary laminated basswood backing strainer that is a reproduction of Georgia O'Keeffe's original design with her post-1954 framer Peter Bayle. The glazing is Optium® tin salt-coated, UV-absorbing, static-free, non-reflective acrylic. The Optium glazing has a Volara closed-cell polyethylene gasket/pad. The frame is fitted with a laminated, Volara-gasketed backing strainer, which has a Security mirror-hanger and T-bolt hardware as well as D-rings.
